properties.label: Recordings and server data: recordings page [CONTEXT_PATH]/blackbox/  ·  Uploaders view and delete their own recordings; see "Who can view and delete every recording". Joget admins follow these settings like everyone else. For every recording that reaches it, the server records the recorded tab's Joget log lines and requests (the extension tags them) and a System Info snapshot (the Info tab), plus the parts ticked below. Server data waits on the server until the recording is uploaded, then is kept with it.

properties.name: canUpload
properties.label: Who can upload
properties.description: Default: Logged In User (any logged-in user; empty means the same). Applies to uploads from the extension and to Import ZIP, also for admins. Uploaders view and delete their own recordings.

properties.name: canCaptureServerData
properties.label: Who can capture and see other users' server data
properties.description: Default: Is Admin (admins only). Empty = nobody. Who may see the server data of other users' recordings, tick "All server log lines" in the extension's popup (every log line the server writes during the recording, also from other users' requests; with virtual hosts, only requests to the recording's own profile, no background jobs) and keep a ZIP's server data on import (a ZIP can hold another user's recording). Everyone's own recordings always get, and show, their own server data.

properties.name: canManageRecordings
properties.label: Who can view and delete every recording
properties.description: Default: Is Admin (admins only). Empty = nobody. They see every user's recording on the recordings page and can download and delete it. A recording's server data shows only to its uploader and to users in "Who can capture and see other users' server data".

properties.name: maxSizeMb
properties.label: Max file size (MB)
properties.description: Applies to the video and to session.json separately. The recorder stops and saves at 90% of it, so the upload fits. A ZIP import may be up to twice this plus 64 MB.
properties.validation_message: Enter a whole number of MB.

properties.name: maxRecordingMinutes
properties.label: Max recording length (minutes)
properties.description: 5 to 120. Applies to every recording: the recorder shows the time left, warns 2 minutes before, and stops and saves the recording at this length. If the browser doesn't stop it, the server ends the capture 2 minutes later, at this length.
properties.validation_message: Enter a whole number of minutes from 5 to 120.

properties.name: userQuotaMb
properties.label: Storage per user (MB)
properties.description: For every user, admins too: what all their recordings may use on the server, counting server data and exported apps. An upload that would go past it is refused; they delete recordings to make room. 0 = no limit.

properties.name: maxOpenCaptures
properties.label: Max recordings in progress per user
properties.description: For every user, admins too: recordings started and not yet stopped (each holds a server capture and a System Info snapshot). A closed browser's recordings stop on their own a few minutes later. 0 = no limit.

properties.name: captureStartsPerMinute
properties.label: Max recordings started per user per minute
properties.description: For every user, admins too; counted on each node. 0 = no limit.

properties.name: importMaxTotalMb
properties.label: Max total size of a ZIP import (MB)
properties.description: Default: empty = 3 x Max file size. If Max file size = 500 MB, Max total size of a ZIP import = 1500 MB. All files of an imported ZIP together, unpacked. Each file also has Max file size. 0 = no limit (a small ZIP can then unpack to many GB).

properties.name: importMaxEntries
properties.label: Max files in a ZIP import
properties.description: Default 5000; empty means the same. 0 = no limit.

properties.name: systemLogMaxMb
properties.label: Max size of system logs per node per recording (MB)
properties.description: Each server node keeps up to this much of a recording's log lines (with the other server log lines when ticked in the popup); later lines are dropped and the viewer says the log was cut off.
properties.validation_message: Enter a whole number of MB.

properties.name: serverDataKeepDays
properties.label: Delete server data not uploaded after (days)
properties.description: Server data of a recording never uploaded (log lines, server load, traces, Info, Glowroot data, exported apps) is deleted after this many days.
properties.validation_message: Enter a whole number of days.

properties.name: allowCaptureGauges
properties.label: Allow capturing server load
properties.description: Applies to admins too. Samples each node the recording reaches every second: heap, GC time, CPU, busy request threads and database connections, shown as the Server load strip. No Glowroot needed. Each recording gets it only when "Capture server load" is ticked in the extension's popup (unticked by default).

properties.name: allowCaptureTraces
properties.label: Allow capturing Glowroot traces of slow and failed requests
properties.description: Applies to admins too. Copies Glowroot's trace of each recorded request Glowroot kept. Needs Glowroot on each node (see "Glowroot address"). Glowroot's own settings decide which requests have a trace (slow or failed); BlackBox doesn't change them. Each recording gets it only when "Capture Glowroot trace files" is ticked in the extension's popup (unticked by default).

properties.name: allowCaptureOtherUsersTraces
properties.label: Allow capturing other users' traces
properties.description: Applies to admins too. Needs "Allow capturing Glowroot traces". About 30 seconds after a recording stops, each node it reached copies the traces Glowroot kept of every other request and background job that ran during the recording (up to 200 per node), listed apart in the Traces tab with the user. With "Capture Glowroot data" the cut then keeps every trace of that time too. They hold other users' data (SQL with values, URLs). Each recording gets them only when "Include other users' traces" is ticked in the extension's popup (unticked by default). With virtual hosts on, it needs the server started with -Dblackbox.sharedGlowroot=true (in its start command; setting it at run time is ignored): Glowroot holds every profile's requests.

properties.name: allowCaptureGlowrootData
properties.label: Allow capturing Glowroot data
properties.description: Applies to admins too. Needs Glowroot 0.14 on each node. 30 to 90 seconds after a recording stops, each node it reached cuts the recording out of its Glowroot data, in Glowroot's own format: the traces of the recorded requests, plus the aggregates and gauges of all traffic during the recording. Download it on the replay page and open it in a standalone Glowroot. Each build needs free disk space in Joget's temp folder of about the size of Glowroot's data.h2.db (it is skipped, with the reason, when there is not enough). Each recording gets it only when "Capture Glowroot data" is ticked in the extension's popup (unticked by default). With virtual hosts on, it needs the server started with -Dblackbox.sharedGlowroot=true (in its start command; setting it at run time is ignored): Glowroot holds every profile's requests.

properties.name: glowrootUrl
properties.label: Glowroot address
properties.description: Default: empty = each node's own Glowroot (found from its admin.json, usually http://localhost:4000). Used for traces and Glowroot data. Set = every node uses this address. Read as Glowroot's anonymous user.

properties.name: secretNames
properties.label: Secret names to mask in System Info
properties.description: One name per line (commas also separate); case doesn't matter. A JVM argument (-Dname=value), system property, datasource key or pool setting whose name contains one is masked, and so is a name=value pair with such a name inside a longer value. * matches anything: pass* = names that start with pass, *key = names that end with key. A line starting with ! is an exception for one whole name: !wflow.systemkey keeps exactly that name unmasked (* at an end leaves that end open: !app.*). Empty = the default list. Values shaped like secrets are masked whatever their name: user:password@ in URLs, Bearer and Basic tokens, JWTs, private keys, Joget-encrypted passwords, AWS, GitHub, Slack, Google and OpenAI-style keys. Applies to recordings started after saving.

properties.name: allowUnmaskedCredentials
properties.label: Allow recording browser secrets unmasked
properties.description: Applies to admins too. Off: the extension masks credentials in every recording before saving it: Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie and CSRF or API key headers, and values whose name has a secret word (password, token, secret, api key...) in URLs, form and JSON bodies and response bodies. On: the popup offers "Record browser secrets unmasked" (unticked by default) for recordings that need them.

properties.name: allowUnmaskedSystemInfo
properties.label: Allow recording System Info secrets unmasked
properties.description: Applies to admins too. Off: the Info tab's JVM arguments, system properties, datasource file and pool settings have their secrets masked (see Secret names to mask in System Info), e.g. smtp.pass. On: the popup offers "Record System Info secrets unmasked" (unticked by default). The database password is never recorded. Separate from Allow recording browser secrets unmasked, which covers the browser's traffic, and from the license option below.

properties.name: allowUnmaskedLicense
properties.label: Allow recording license secrets unmasked
properties.description: Enterprise only (Community has no license table). Applies to admins too. Off: the Info tab's License section shows the system key (platform.systemKey), the license signature (platform.license.signature, the system key the license was issued for) and the MAC address (platform.net.address) as ****; the rest of the license table is shown as System Info shows it. On: the popup offers "Record license secrets unmasked" (unticked by default).

properties.name: allowHttpUpload
properties.label: Allow uploads over HTTP
properties.description: Off: uploads, imports and server captures must use HTTPS (or a proxy that sends X-Forwarded-Proto: https); a server reached as localhost is always allowed. Recordings can hold passwords and personal data, which plain HTTP sends readable by anyone on the network.

properties.name: allowArmedRecordings
properties.label: Allow recordings that start before login
properties.description: For problems on the login page, single sign-on (SAML, OIDC) or anonymous pages. On: a user in Who can upload clicks "Prepare a recording that starts logged out" in the popup while logged in, logs out, and starts recording within the minutes set below; the server data of that recording belongs to them. The prepared one-time token works once, only from the extension, and can't read or upload anything. Off: recordings started while logged out have no server data.

properties.name: armTokenMinutes
properties.label: Before-login recordings expire after (minutes)
properties.description: 1 to 60. How long a recording prepared with "Prepare a recording that starts logged out" waits to be started; unused, it expires. Shorter is safer: the one-time token opens a server capture for whoever holds it. A change applies to recordings prepared after it.
properties.validation_message: Enter a whole number of minutes from 1 to 60.

properties.name: allowUnsandboxedTraces
properties.label: Allow unsandboxed trace pages in HTML exports
properties.description: On: Open full trace in a downloaded .html file opens the Glowroot page as it is, like opening the trace file itself (for internal review). Off: it opens inside a sandbox, so a crafted trace page can't reach the site the file is opened from. The recordings page always sandboxes trace pages.

properties.name: allowedExtensionIds
properties.label: Allowed Chrome extension IDs
properties.description: Comma-separated. Only these extensions may send recordings without a CSRF token; any other extension is refused. The BlackBox extension's own ID is anmfmkacddnmmgdcnkgkfjhagnilmkmp (the same on every computer). Empty = any extension.

properties.label: Support data: the apps the recording used, their data, and the recent changes in the Info tab.

properties.name: recentChangesDays
properties.label: Recent changes period (days)
properties.description: The Info tab's first section lists the app versions and wflow files changed in this period (the app versions narrowed to the apps the recording used and apps sharing their tables). Taken at recording start, with the System Info snapshot. At most 365.

properties.name: allowAppExport
properties.label: Allow exporting the apps used in the recording
properties.description: Applies to admins too. When the recording stops (or at upload, when there was no capture or that export failed), the apps found in the recorded tab's URLs (apps with problems first, then the most used; App Center only when it had problems or was the only app) are exported with Joget's own app export (.jwa, without form data, plugins or groups) and kept with the recording. Whose apps: see "Who can export apps they don't administer". Each recording gets it only when "Export the apps used" is ticked in the extension's popup (unticked by default). App definitions can hold plugin settings and environment variables.

properties.name: maxApps
properties.label: Max apps to export
properties.description: Per recording. Apps the user may not have exported don't count. 0 = no limit; empty or not a whole number up to 9999 = 3.

properties.name: canExportOtherApps
properties.label: Who can export apps they don't administer
properties.description: Default: Is Admin (admins only). Empty = nobody. Users chosen here get only the apps Joget lets them access (one of the app's userviews allows them); other apps are listed as not exported.

properties.name: allowAppAdminExport
properties.label: Allow app admins to export their own apps
properties.description: On (default): an app's own admins (ROLE_ADMIN and ROLE_ADMIN_GROUP in the app's app.properties; on Joget 9, also the app creator who created it) get that app exported, with its data when apps data is captured. Off: nobody gets an app for being its admin; only "Who can export apps they don't administer" and "Allow apps data from apps they don't administer" decide. A Joget admin is not an app's admin unless the app lists them.

properties.name: allowOtherAppsData
properties.label: Allow apps data from apps they don't administer
properties.description: For users exporting an app they are not an admin of (see Who can export apps they don't administer), and for app admins when "Allow app admins to export their own apps" is off. Off: that app's definition is exported without its rows and process data. Record ids come from the uploaded recording, so with this on a user can pick which rows of the app get exported.

properties.name: allowCaptureAppsData
properties.label: Allow capturing apps data
properties.description: Applies to admins too. Rows added to each exported .jwa like Joget's own export with data, so importing it imports them: the records the recording opened or saved, rows linked to them, and the newest rows of tables with none; plus the processes the recording touched (read only). Real values and original record ids, except always-masked columns; uploaded files up to 5 MB each, 50 MB per app (larger ones become placeholders). Each recording gets it only when "Capture apps data" is ticked in the extension's popup (unticked by default). Shown here only when "Allow apps data from apps they don't administer" is ticked; hidden, it keeps its value, which still applies to app admins' own apps.

properties.name: allowMaskData
properties.label: Allow masking apps data
properties.description: Applies to admins too. Shows "Mask data" in the extension's popup (unticked by default). Ticked there, all apps data is masked: letters and digits get fakes of the same kind, so length and format stay; record ids (primary keys) get new ones, also where other rows point at them, so importing never overwrites rows (the App tab lists old and new ids); process data and user names (user1, user2...) are masked too; uploaded files become placeholders. Kept: option values, yes/no/true/false, numbers up to 5 digits, UUIDs, process ids and values in the app definition; dates keep their year. Without the box, apps data is real.

properties.name: sampleRows
properties.label: Newest rows per table when the recording touched none
properties.description: Per app table. At most 500.

properties.name: sensitiveColumns
properties.label: Always-masked column names
properties.description: One word per line (commas also separate). A column whose name has one as a word (ic_no, homeAddress, email-2) is always masked, also when Mask data is not ticked. Empty = the default list.
